title: The Store Called Leslie's: Kingsdale, New Albany, and the Power of Attorney
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Dayton, the birth
stops.date_confidence: attested; Wikipedia, 'Les Wexner' gives 8 September 1937 and the parents' names
stops.campa: Leslie Herbert Wexner is born in Dayton to Harry and Bella Wexner. His mother was born Bella Cabakoff in the Williamsburg district of Brooklyn, into a family of Russian Jewish immigrants who came west; his father sells clothing for other men, on another man's floor. Ohio in 1937 is a state of factory towns and department stores, and the trade the boy is born into is the plainest one in it: buy a garment, mark it up, hang it where a woman will see it. He will spend nearly his whole life inside a hundred miles of it.
suggested_refs: Dayton, Ohio, birthplace recorded in every biographical summary of Wexner and in no primary document reached

stops.name: Bexley, the shop called Leslie's
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the shop and the suburb are attested, the year 1951 is not. It comes from the crawled dossier and Britannica-derived summaries and could not be traced to a source that states it
stops.campa: The family settles in Bexley, a suburb east of Columbus, and opens a women's clothing store named for the son. Harry Wexner sells coats and dresses, the slow half of the floor, and keeps the books the way a man keeps them when a bad season can close him. Bella runs the register. The son's name is over the door and his opinion is not asked for inside it. He grows up between the two of them, after school and on Saturdays, learning what sells and what sits, and hearing his father say which is which.
stops.quote: I had decided quite subconsciously that I was going to prove to my dad that I had real worth and I could do something, but the only language he understood was the business he was in.
stops.quote_source: Leslie H. Wexner, 'Victoria's Other Secret,' Academy of Achievement interview, Columbus, Ohio, 10 February 2017
suggested_refs: The store called Leslie's, Bexley, Ohio, the family business named for the subject

stops.name: Bexley High School, the years on Cassingham Road
stops.date_confidence: attendance attested by Wikipedia, 'Bexley High School,' which lists him among notable alumni; the specific years are inferred backward from his 1955 enrolment at Ohio State and are not stated in any source reached
stops.campa: He attends the public high school at 326 South Cassingham Road, four blocks from the family store. Bexley is a well-off suburb and the school is a good one, and nothing in the record of these years distinguishes him from any other Ohio boy whose parents keep a shop. No teacher from these years is remembered in anything he has said since, and no prize is recorded. The school lists him among its notable alumni, which is where the attendance is documented. The four years are otherwise blank.
suggested_refs: Bexley High School, 326 South Cassingham Road, Bexley, Ohio

stops.name: The Oval, Ohio State University
stops.date_confidence: attested for entry and for the 1959 business degree; the September start date is the ordinary academic one and is not separately sourced
stops.campa: He enrolls at Ohio State, joins the Sigma Alpha Mu fraternity, and takes a business degree in 1959. The campus is enormous and public and eight miles from Bexley, close enough that the store is still the fixed point of his week. What he studies is what the store does, formalized: inventory, turns, margin. The Oval is the open green at the center of the campus, and he crosses it four years running. He is a competent student and not a remarkable one.
suggested_refs: The Ohio State University, class of 1959, business degree

stops.name: Drinko Hall, the law school he leaves
stops.date_confidence: attested that he briefly attended the Moritz College of Law (Wikipedia, 'Les Wexner'); the start date is inferred from the 1959 graduation and no source gives the length of the attendance
stops.campa: He starts law school at Ohio State and does not finish it. Drinko Hall has housed the college for one year when he walks into it. No source reached says how long he stayed, what he studied, or why he left, and he has never given the departure a story in any interview that survives. There is a period after this in which he serves in the Air National Guard, and not one document reached names the base. Then he is back on the sales floor of his father's store, arguing about what to stock.
suggested_refs: Moritz College of Law, Drinko Hall, Ohio State University, housing the college since 1958

segments.name: Kingsdale, and the Bet on the Fast Half of the Floor

stops.name: Kingsdale Shopping Center, the first Limited
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; Wikipedia, 'L Brands'
stops.campa: On the tenth of August he opens a single store in a suburban shopping center in Upper Arlington, on about five thousand dollars borrowed from an aunt and five thousand more from a bank. The argument with his father is the whole business plan: coats and dresses sit, sportswear moves, so stock only the half that moves. He calls the store The Limited because that is literally what it is, a store limited to one thing. First-year sales come to a hundred and sixty-two thousand dollars.
suggested_refs: Kingsdale Shopping Center, Upper Arlington, Ohio, site of the first Limited store
sources: FundingUniverse, company history of The Limited

stops.name: Columbus, the second store
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month; Wikipedia, 'Les Wexner'. Pinned at the Columbus centroid because no source reached gives the street address
stops.campa: A year after the first, a second Limited opens in Columbus. The model has proved itself in twelve months, and from here the only question he will ask for four decades is how fast the same store can be copied. Two stores in one city, stocked from one set of buying decisions, is already the whole method, and the method does not change again. His father, who told him the idea was wrong, comes to work for him. Neither of them is recorded saying anything about that.
suggested_refs: The second Limited store, Columbus, Ohio, August 1964

stops.name: Columbus, the shares sold over the counter
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year only; month and day defaulted. The Limited sold 47,600 shares at $7.25 in 1969, traded over the counter, and was not listed on the New York Stock Exchange until 1982. Draft chronologies that placed this event on Wall Street in 1969 are wrong and are corrected here
stops.campa: Six years after Kingsdale the company sells forty-seven thousand six hundred shares at seven dollars and twenty-five cents. There is no floor and no bell: the stock trades over the counter, quoted by dealers who telephone each other. Wexner keeps control and takes on the one obligation that will shape everything after, which is that a public company must grow every quarter or explain why it did not. Thirteen years will pass before the shares are listed in New York.
suggested_refs: The 1969 over-the-counter offering of The Limited, 47,600 shares at $7.25
sources: FundingUniverse, company history of The Limited

stops.name: Columbus, the chairmanship
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year only; month and day defaulted. The pin is an acknowledged placeholder: no source reached gives the address of the company's offices in 1975, and the downtown centroid is used in the absence of one
stops.campa: Twelve years after the first store he becomes chairman of the board of the company he founded, which by now runs across several states. He is thirty-seven. He will hold the chief executive's office for fifty-seven years, one of the longest such tenures on record in the country. He holds it by never delegating the one decision that matters to him, which is what hangs on the rack. The address of the offices he chairs from in 1975 is not in any source reached.
suggested_refs: The Limited Inc., Columbus, Ohio, board chairmanship from 1975
sources: EBSCO/company biographical summary via research dossier

stops.name: Morse Road, the headquarters
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; Wikipedia, 'Bath & Body Works, Inc.' The coordinates are approximate to the Morse Road corridor in north Columbus and are not a surveyed corporate address
stops.campa: The company moves its headquarters out to Morse Road in north Columbus, onto ground with room to grow into, and it will stay on that road for the rest of the century. It is a campus rather than a tower: low buildings, parking, distribution close by. The state capitol is eight miles south. Every acquisition of the next twenty years, a lingerie chain in California, a hunting outfitter in New York, eight hundred Lerner shops, is absorbed into this address.
suggested_refs: The Morse Road headquarters campus, north Columbus, occupied from 1977

stops.name: Andover, Mast Industries and the debt
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year only; month and day defaulted. The coordinates are the town of Andover, Massachusetts, not a pinned corporate address for Mast Industries
stops.campa: He buys Mast Industries, a sourcing company in Andover, Massachusetts, and takes on serious debt to do it. Mast holds the contracts, the shipping, and the factories in Asia. Buying it means the company no longer waits on other people's suppliers to decide what it can sell. From here the design, the manufacture, the freight, and the sales floor answer to one office in Ohio. None of that shows in a store window. The board is frightened by the borrowing and says so.
stops.quote_source: Leslie H. Wexner, Academy of Achievement interview, Columbus, Ohio, 10 February 2017
suggested_refs: Mast Industries, Andover, Massachusetts, acquired 1978 to build vertical sourcing

stops.name: New York Stock Exchange, the listing
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year only; month and day defaulted. Wikipedia, 'Bath & Body Works, Inc.': 'In 1982, The Limited was first listed on the New York Stock Exchange'
stops.campa: The Limited is listed on the New York Stock Exchange, thirteen years after the over-the-counter offering that a good deal of later writing mistakes for this moment. A Columbus retailer of women's sportswear now trades on the floor at Broad and Wall alongside the steel and oil companies. No source reached gives the month. The listed shares are a currency he can spend without cash. In the same year he spends more than four hundred million dollars buying other people's stores.
suggested_refs: The New York Stock Exchange, 11 Wall Street, where The Limited was first listed in 1982

stops.name: Columbus, Lane Bryant bought whole
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year only; month and day defaulted. Wikipedia, 'L Brands'
stops.campa: He buys Lane Bryant, two hundred and seven stores, for about a hundred and five million dollars. Lane Bryant was founded by a widow named Lena Bryant who sewed maternity dresses in New York and built a national chain out of clothing the trade had ignored. Wexner does not need her buildings or her buyers. He needs the name over the door and the racks inside it, which the Ohio office can restock in a season. Seventy years of customers already trust the sign.
suggested_refs: Lane Bryant, acquired 1982, roughly 207 stores for about $105 million

stops.name: Columbus, Victoria's Secret for a million dollars
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year only; month and day defaulted. Wikipedia, 'L Brands', 'Les Wexner', and 'Victoria's Secret'
stops.campa: He buys Victoria's Secret from Roy and Gaye Raymond for stock and about a million dollars. What he buys is five or six stores in California and a mail-order catalog, a strained business its founder can no longer carry. What he sees in it is not underwear but a room: a store designed entirely from the customer's side, where the fittings and the fabric and the light are all arranged around one person who is not the man who owns it. Raymond designed that room and is selling it under financial strain.
stops.quote: This is a ladies' paradise... It's all about her.
stops.quote_source: Leslie H. Wexner on the Victoria's Secret concept, Academy of Achievement interview, Columbus, Ohio, 10 February 2017. The full passage runs: 'This is a ladies' paradise. And that thinking goes into the design of the store, the fitting rooms, the fabric, the display. It's all from the lady's point of view. It has nothing to do with men... It's all about her.'
suggested_refs: Roy and Gaye Raymond's original Victoria's Secret, founded at the Stanford Shopping Center, Palo Alto, 12 June 1977, and sold under financial strain in 1982

stops.name: New York, Henri Bendel and Lerner Shops
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year only; month and day defaulted. Wikipedia, 'L Brands'
stops.campa: In one year he takes Henri Bendel for about ten million dollars and Lerner Shops, seven hundred and ninety-eight stores, for about two hundred and ninety-seven million. Bendel is a small Fifth Avenue house with a reputation for taste; Lerner is cheap clothing in eight hundred American towns. He wants both, for the same reason he wanted Lane Bryant: a name that already means something is cheaper to buy than to build. What goes on the racks afterward is decided on Morse Road.
suggested_refs: Henri Bendel and Lerner Shops, both acquired by The Limited in 1985

stops.name: Columbus, Abercrombie and Fitch, and a seat on the board of trustees
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year only; month and day defaulted. Wikipedia, 'L Brands' for the acquisition, Wikipedia, 'Les Wexner' for the first trustee term, which runs 1988 to 1997
stops.campa: He buys Abercrombie and Fitch for about forty-six million dollars. It is a hundred-year-old outfitter that sold rifles to Theodore Roosevelt and is now twenty-five failing stores; he will empty it out and refill it with clothes for teenagers. What he pays for is the century in the name; the stock on the shelves is worth nothing to him. In the same year he takes his first seat as a trustee of Ohio State University, the school whose law college he walked out of, a term that runs to 1997. He is fifty.
suggested_refs: Abercrombie & Fitch, acquired 1988, about 25 stores for about $46 million
Wexner's Ohio State trusteeship, first term 1988 to 1997

stops.name: Palm Beach, the introduction
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year only; month and day defaulted. The circumstances are contradicted between sources and the contradiction is not resolved: Wikipedia, 'Jeffrey Epstein' places the introduction at Palm Beach through unnamed mutual acquaintances, while the research dossier names the insurance executive Robert Meister and his wife as the connectors and gives no location at all
stops.campa: In Florida he is introduced to a former schoolteacher turned financier named Jeffrey Epstein. The two accounts of who made the introduction do not agree: one says mutual acquaintances in Palm Beach, the other names an insurance executive and his wife and gives no place. Wexner is forty-eight and worth more money than his own accountants can keep tidy. Epstein is thirty-three, has no clients anyone can name, and tells people he takes only billionaires.
stops.quote: I first met Mr. Epstein in the mid-1980s, through friends who vouched for and recommended him as a knowledgeable financial professional.
stops.quote_source: Leslie Wexner, 'Letter from Les,' The Wexner Foundation, 8 August 2019
suggested_refs: The 1986 introduction, dated but not located in agreement by any two sources reached

stops.name: New York, the man who untangles the finances
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year only; month and day defaulted. Wikipedia, 'Jeffrey Epstein'
stops.campa: Within a year Epstein has become his financial adviser and then something with no title: the man who answers for the money. Wexner's affairs are complicated, spread across a public company, private holdings, real estate, and a family. Epstein reduces them to order in about twelve months and makes himself indispensable doing it. He has no other client anyone at the company can name, and nobody at the company asks. What exactly he does for the money is a question the record never answers.
suggested_refs: Epstein's engagement as Wexner's financial adviser from 1987

stops.name: 9 East 71st Street, the Straus mansion
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; Wikipedia, '9 East 71st Street'. The coordinates are inherited byte-identical from the existing Epstein and Maxwell files so that three journeys stand on one dot; Wikipedia's own figure for the building is 40.77155, -73.96654, about 130 m away, and the discrepancy is recorded in the report
stops.campa: He buys the unfinished Herbert N. Straus house on the Upper East Side for thirteen million two hundred thousand dollars. Horace Trumbauer designed it and it was completed in 1932; it is one of the largest private houses in Manhattan and it has never been properly lived in. Wexner does not move into it either. Within a few years Jeffrey Epstein is occupying it and presenting it to visitors as his own, and the title will not formally pass to an Epstein-controlled entity until 2011, for no recorded payment.
suggested_refs: 9 East 71st Street, Manhattan, sold in March 2021 for $51 million with the proceeds directed to the Epstein Victims' Compensation Program

stops.name: Columbus, the power of attorney
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month; Wikipedia, 'Jeffrey Epstein'. Day defaulted. Pinned at Columbus, where the instrument was executed
stops.campa: In July he signs a document giving Jeffrey Epstein comprehensive power of attorney: authority to hire people, sign checks, buy and sell property, borrow money, and enter transactions that bind Leslie Wexner in law. It is four years after the first engagement, and it stays in force for sixteen. The instrument is executed in Ohio, in the city where he has lived and worked his whole adult life. The houses, the aircraft, and the fortune nobody could ever source all date from after this signature.
suggested_refs: The July 1991 power of attorney, acknowledged by Wexner in his February 2026 congressional deposition

stops.name: New Albany, the marriage to Abigail Koppel
stops.date_confidence: the date is attested to the day (Wikipedia, 'Les Wexner'); the venue is not established and the sources conflict. One lens gives 'probably New York area, exact venue not specified,' another infers New Albany. The stop is pinned at his Ohio residence and asserts no venue. A direct fetch of Abigail Wexner's page returned no result
stops.campa: He marries Abigail S. Koppel, a lawyer, in a small ceremony. He is fifty-five and she is thirty-one. Where the ceremony took place is not established by anything reachable; the sources that mention it at all disagree, and one gives no place. The dossier says Epstein helped arrange the prenuptial agreement and attended, and no independent source reached confirms either detail. Abigail Wexner will become a public figure in Ohio in her own right. The venue stays blank.
suggested_refs: The 23 January 1993 marriage, dated in every summary and located in none of them

stops.name: Rickenbacker, the cargo airline comes to Columbus
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year only; month and day defaulted. Wikipedia, 'Southern Air Transport'
stops.campa: Southern Air Transport moves its world headquarters to Rickenbacker, the old air base south of Columbus. The airline was owned by the Central Intelligence Agency until 1973 and had flown for it long after; by now it hauls freight, and much of what it carries from Hong Kong to Columbus is bound for The Limited. That is the whole of the documented relation: a cargo contract between a retailer and a carrier with a history. What later writers build on top of it, that the two men were intelligence assets, has no authenticated public record behind it.
suggested_refs: Southern Air Transport, CIA-owned until 1973, headquartered at Rickenbacker from 1995

segments.name: The Foundation, the Center, the Town

stops.name: Columbus, the Wexner Foundation
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year only; month and day defaulted. Wikipedia, 'Wexner Foundation.' A draft chronology conflated this with the Wexner Heritage Program, which is a separate thing launched in 1985 with Rabbi Herbert A. Friedman; the two are kept apart here
stops.campa: He establishes the Wexner Foundation. Two years later its first core program opens, the Wexner Heritage Program, built with Rabbi Herbert A. Friedman to take Jewish communal leaders out of their committees and put them through several years of serious study. It is not relief and it is not building funds. What the money buys is a leadership class for American Jewry, made one cohort at a time, in seminars, over years. Its alumni run institutions across the country forty years later.
stops.quote: For 35 years, the work we have achieved together in this community has continued to be one of the great honors of my life
stops.quote_source: Leslie Wexner, 'Letter from Les,' addressed to the Wexner Foundation network, 8 August 2019
suggested_refs: The Wexner Heritage Program, launched 1985 with Rabbi Herbert A. Friedman

stops.name: Harvard Kennedy School, the Israel Fellowship
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year only; month and day defaulted. Wikipedia, 'Wexner Foundation': the program was created in 1989 as a partnership with Harvard University's Kennedy School of Government
stops.campa: The Wexner Israel Fellowship begins on the riverfront campus at Cambridge, a partnership with Harvard's Kennedy School that takes up to ten mid-career Israeli public officials a year and puts them through a master's degree in public administration. Over the decades more than two hundred and eighty pass through, and they return to ministries, city halls, and general staffs. It is the one part of his philanthropy that operates outside the United States, and it runs for thirty-four years before he ends it.
suggested_refs: The Wexner Israel Fellowship at the Harvard Kennedy School, 1989 to 2023, ended by the Foundation in October 2023
sources: research dossier (the October 2023 termination, not independently fetched)

stops.name: Wexner Center for the Arts, the opening
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; Wikipedia, 'Wexner Center for the Arts'
stops.campa: The arts center opens on North High Street on the Ohio State campus. Peter Eisenman designed it with Richard Trott and Laurie Olin laid out the ground, and the building is deconstructivist: a white scaffold that cuts across the campus grid at an angle, with columns that stop before they reach the floor. It is named for Harry Wexner, the father who sold coats and dresses and said the idea was wrong. The son put twenty-five million dollars into a forty-three million dollar building to do it.
suggested_refs: The Wexner Center for the Arts, 1871 North High Street, Columbus, opened 17 November 1989, named for Harry Wexner

stops.name: New Albany, the house on three hundred and thirty-six acres
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; Wikipedia, 'Les Wexner.' Coordinates are approximate: the exact address of the estate is not public. The associated claim that he formed The New Albany Company with the developer Jack Kessler in 1990 is reconstruction, unconfirmed by any source reached
stops.campa: He builds a thirty-room Georgian house on three hundred and thirty-six acres at New Albany, a village northeast of Columbus, and begins buying the country around it. The house is later valued at about forty-seven million dollars. What he is making is not a residence but a town: roads, schools, white fences, a company that assembles the land. An annual equestrian competition runs on the grounds for benefit of a child-safety center until 2018. The gate is guarded and the estate does not appear on public maps.
suggested_refs: The Wexner estate, New Albany, Ohio, built c. 1990 on roughly 336 acres

stops.name: New Albany, Bath and Body Works
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year for the founding at New Albany; month and day defaulted. Wikipedia, 'Bath & Body Works.' The first store opened in September 1990 in a Cambridge, Massachusetts mall, not in Ohio, and drafts that placed the first store in Columbus are corrected here
stops.campa: Bath and Body Works is founded at New Albany as a beauty line for Express, and its first store opens that September in a shopping mall in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Soap, lotion, and a shop that smells from the sidewalk. It costs almost nothing to start and is not bought from anybody. Of everything the company will own, this is the one thing built from the ground rather than acquired with a name attached. Thirty-one years later it is still trading under that name.
suggested_refs: Bath & Body Works, founded 1990 at New Albany, Ohio; first store Cambridge, Massachusetts, September 1990

stops.name: Columbus, the brand at a billion dollars
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year only; month and day defaulted. Wikipedia, 'L Brands'
stops.campa: Ten years after he bought it for about a million dollars, Victoria's Secret passes a billion dollars in annual sales. Ten years earlier it was five or six stores in California and a mail-order list. The catalog now goes to tens of millions of households. It is the largest lingerie retailer in the country. The name over the door still belongs to a fictional Englishwoman invented in California in 1977 by a man who could not make the business work, and the room inside it has been rebuilt from Ohio.
suggested_refs: Victoria's Secret at roughly $1 billion in sales, 1992

segments.name: What Was Reported on the Property

stops.name: Columbus, Abercrombie and Fitch cut loose
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year only; month and day defaulted. Wikipedia, 'Abercrombie & Fitch' and 'Bath & Body Works, Inc.' both give 1996 for the spin-off as a separate public company. The claim that the remaining stake was distributed tax-free in 1998, which a draft chronology gave as the spin-off date, is reconstruction and is not stated by any source reached
stops.campa: Abercrombie and Fitch is spun off as a separate public company, eight years after he bought the wreck of it, twenty-five stores, for forty-six million dollars. Under Mike Jeffries it has become the most aggressive teenage brand in America, and it is now worth many times what it cost. The method is the one he has run since Lane Bryant: buy a dead name cheap, refill it, sell what the market will price. He keeps a stake and distributes the rest two years later.
suggested_refs: Abercrombie & Fitch, spun off as an independent public company in 1996

stops.name: New Albany, the guest house
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month for Maria Farmer's arrival; day defaulted. Wikipedia, 'Maria Farmer' confirms the May 1996 travel to the Wexner property, the 10,600 square foot guest home, the artist-in-residence arrangement, the NYPD report in August 1996 and the FBI report in September 1996. The dossier's further claim that the guest house had been deeded to Epstein in 1992 could not be confirmed anywhere reachable and is not asserted
stops.campa: On the Wexner estate stands a guest house of ten thousand six hundred square feet. In May the artist Maria Farmer travels to Ohio and is installed in it as an artist in residence, an arrangement Jeffrey Epstein made. She states that Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell sexually assaulted her there. She reports it to the New York police in August and to the Federal Bureau of Investigation in September. Wexner says he does not know her and did not know of Epstein's abuse. No finding has ever placed him in that house.
suggested_refs: Washington Post investigations by Jonathan O'Connell and Sarah Ellison into Maria Farmer and the New Albany property, 2019, cited through the research dossier and not independently fetched

stops.name: Foxcote House, the English county estate
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; Wikipedia, 'Foxcote House': 'sold by them in 1997 to the American billionaire Les Wexner.' Month and day defaulted
stops.campa: He buys Foxcote House near Ilmington in Warwickshire, an English country estate in the hills above the Stour. It is the only property he holds outside the United States, and the family that held it before him sold in that year. For thirty-four years he has sold American women a version of England: the catalogs, the shop windows, a brand named for a queen who never existed. Now he owns a house in the actual country and puts a fence around it. Nothing in the record says how often he goes there.
suggested_refs: Foxcote House, Ilmington, Warwickshire, purchased 1997

stops.name: New York, the magazine profile
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year; month and day defaulted. Vicky Ward's 'The Talented Mr. Epstein' ran in Vanity Fair in 2003. The reported removal of the Farmer sisters' allegations from the piece before publication is carried from the research dossier and was not independently fetched. Vanity Fair blocked direct fetch this pass; the Wexner phrase below reaches this file through PBS NewsHour's February 2026 relay of it, not through the original text
stops.campa: Vicky Ward publishes a profile of Jeffrey Epstein in Vanity Fair, asking where the money comes from and finding, at the end of every thread, Leslie Wexner. Allegations from Maria and Annie Farmer were reportedly cut from the piece before it ran, under legal pressure. Wexner is quoted in it about Epstein in the register a client uses about a professional, and the two words that do the work are judgment and standards. The piece runs in 2003 and nothing follows from it for sixteen years.
stops.quote: excellent judgment and unusually high standards
stops.quote_source: Leslie Wexner on Jeffrey Epstein, Vanity Fair, 'The Talented Mr. Epstein,' 2003, as relayed by PBS NewsHour, February 2026
suggested_refs: Vicky Ward, 'The Talented Mr. Epstein,' Vanity Fair, 2003
sources: research dossier (the removal of the Farmer allegations, unconfirmed)

stops.name: Columbus, the accounts closed
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the year rests on Wexner's own later account in the 2019 letter and on reporting summarizing it. No independent contemporaneous documentation of a 2007 termination was found. Month and day defaulted
stops.campa: By his own account he decides in this year to end the relationship, and then discovers that Epstein had taken vast sums from him and from his family. Sixteen years of power of attorney close. What was taken has never been stated in an audited figure by anyone; the following year about forty-six million dollars in securities moves from Epstein-controlled entities to a charitable fund, which Wexner will later describe as recovery. The only record of the decision itself is the word of the man who made it.
stops.quote: It appears Epstein was furious that Mr. Wexner refused to meet with him years after Mr. Wexner terminated Epstein and cut off all ties with him following Mr. Wexner's discovery of Epstein's theft and criminal conduct.
stops.quote_source: Tom Davies, spokesperson for Leslie Wexner, quoted in PBS NewsHour, February 2026
suggested_refs: The 2008 transfer of about $46 million in securities to the YLK Charitable Fund, a press-derived figure with no audited disclosure behind it

stops.name: Columbus, the email after the plea
stops.date_confidence: the email is attested to the year 2008 and quoted by PBS NewsHour from released Epstein-files material; month, day, and place are not established and are defaulted, the pin being Wexner's own city. Only the PBS summary of the document was seen, not the scanned original
stops.campa: Epstein pleads guilty in Florida state court to procuring a minor for prostitution and serves thirteen months under an arrangement that lets him leave for work six days a week. In the same year Wexner, who says he cut all ties the year before, writes to him. The message is short, it mentions what Abigail told him, and it is not the language of a man addressing a stranger. It tells Jeffrey Epstein that he broke his own first rule, which was to be careful.
stops.quote: Abigail told me the result… all I can say is I feel sorry. You violated your own number 1 rule … always be careful
stops.quote_source: Leslie Wexner, 2008 email to Jeffrey Epstein, quoted in PBS NewsHour, February 2026. The ellipses are the outlet's
suggested_refs: Epstein's 2008 Florida guilty plea and non-prosecution agreement, West Palm Beach

stops.name: Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center, the hundred million
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day for the announcement; Wikipedia, 'Les Wexner.' The board vote renaming the medical center took effect 10 February 2012
stops.campa: He pledges a hundred million dollars to Ohio State, the largest gift the university has announced, chiefly for the medical center and the cancer hospital. A year later the trustees vote to put his name on the building. He had sat on that board from 1988 to 1997, again from 2005, and chaired it from 2009. The university physician Richard Strauss abused students through 1998, and an independent investigation would later find the university failed to stop him.
suggested_refs: The Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center, 410 West 10th Avenue, Columbus, renamed 10 February 2012

stops.name: Columbus, the company renamed L Brands
